title: Zhuge Liang Executes Ma Su in Tears
text:
In 228 Zhuge Liang, chancellor of the Shu Han kingdom, launched his first northern campaign against the rival kingdom of Wei. For the key post of Jieting, guarding his army's flank, he chose Ma Su, a talented young officer he valued highly, over more experienced generals. Before his death, the Shu founder Liu Bei had warned Zhuge Liang that Ma Su's words exceeded his real abilities.

At Jieting Ma Su ignored Zhuge Liang's instructions and the advice of his deputy Wang Ping. He left the road and camped on a hill away from water. The Wei general Zhang He cut off his water supply and routed his army. The loss of Jieting forced Zhuge Liang to abandon the whole campaign.

Ma Su was condemned to death. Chen Shou's history records his death, and later sources cited in Pei Songzhi's commentary say that Zhuge Liang wept for him and took care of his family.

Zhuge Liang also blamed himself. He wrote to the emperor that the defeat came from his own poor choice of commander and asked to be demoted three grades. The request was granted, though he kept his duties.
lesson: Hold people accountable even when you like them, and own your part in putting them where they failed.
people: Zhuge Liang, Ma Su, Wang Ping
source: Chen Shou, Records of the Three Kingdoms (Sanguozhi), Biographies of Zhuge Liang and Ma Su, with Pei Songzhi's commentary
caveat: One passage in the Sanguozhi says Ma Su died in prison rather than by execution.
